newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close firm led by 2nd tier risers.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close firm led by 2nd tier risers.

text.p: Brazil stocks shrugged off Wall Street's losses to end higher Monday in strong trade and led by second-tier shares, as mostly local investors bought to adjust portfolios ahead of month's end, brokers said.
"The market was firm at the close," one local dealer said. "Local money kept coming in."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 48 most-traded shares closed up 0.97 percent at 12,239 points on trade totalling 786 million reais ($731 million).
Benchmark blue chip Telebras preferred rose 0.39 percent ro end at 156.30 reais while its connom voting share ended 0.71 percent higher at 141.50 reais.
State oil monopoly Petrobras preferred closed 1.71 percent higher at 297 reais and iron miner Cia vale do Rio Doce's preferred ended up 0.84 percent at 23.90 reais.
Power shares continued their strong rises of recent weeks on optimism regarding the sector's privatization.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index ended up 1.08 percent at 3,325 points, led by hikes in Sao Paulo state owned Cia Paulista de Forca e Luz's (CPFL) common and preferred.
CPFL's common rose 4.42 percent to end at 189 reais while the preferred issue jumped 4.35 percent to end at 168 reais.
Brokers said they expect the market to stay its present upside course at least until Thursday when investors may begin to take profits to close out their June books.
